title: Kiedy byłaś młoda…
focus: family stories: past habits, virile and non-virile plurals, żeby

lines.speaker: Kasia
lines.pl: Babciu|babciu, a jak wyglądały|wygladaly niedzielne|niedzielne obiady, kiedy byłaś|bylas młoda|mloda?
lines.en: Grandma, what were Sunday dinners like when you were young?

lines.speaker: Babcia
lines.pl: Zupełnie inaczej. Mieszkaliśmy|mieszkalismy na wsi|wsi, a przy|przy stole siadało|siadalo nas czternaścioro|czternascioro.
lines.en: Completely different. We lived in the countryside, and fourteen of us sat down at the table.

lines.speaker: Babcia
lines.pl: Mięso jedliśmy|jedlismy tylko w niedzielę|niedziele. Mama wstawała|wstawala o piątej|piatej, żeby|zeby upiec|upiec chleb.
lines.en: We only ate meat on Sundays. My mother got up at five to bake bread.

lines.speaker: Wujek Jurek
lines.pl: A ja pamiętam, jak dziadek co tydzień opowiadał|opowiadal tę|te samą historię|historie o wojsku|wojsku.
lines.en: And I remember Grandpa telling the same army story every week.

lines.speaker: Babcia
lines.pl: Bo za każdym razem|razem była trochę inna! Dziadek lubił, żeby|zeby2 wszyscy|wszyscy go słuchali|sluchali.
lines.en: Because it was a bit different every time! Grandpa liked everyone to listen to him.

lines.speaker: Ania
lines.pl: A teraz wszyscy siedzą przy stole z telefonami|telefonami.
lines.en: And now everyone sits at the table with their phones.

lines.speaker: Babcia
lines.pl: Dlatego dziś proponuję zasadę|zasade: kto pierwszy weźmie|wezmie telefon do ręki|reki, ten zmywa|zmywa naczynia.
lines.en: That’s why today I propose a rule: whoever picks up their phone first does the washing-up.

lines.speaker: Kasia
lines.pl: Ale ja tylko sprawdzałam|sprawdzalam przepis|przepis na sernik!
lines.en: But I was only checking the cheesecake recipe!

babciu.why: Nouns in -ia take -u in the vocative: babcia → babciu, ciocia → ciociu, Kasia → Kasiu.

wygladaly.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 3rd person plural · non-virile
wygladaly.why: Obiady is a masculine noun, but it doesn’t refer to men, so the plural is non-virile: obiady wyglądały. Only groups that include male persons take virile -li.

niedzielne.why: An adjective formed from niedziela. Polish often uses an adjective where English uses a noun as a modifier: niedzielny obiad, “Sunday dinner.”

bylas.why: Kasia addresses her grandmother with ty, as Polish families do, so the verb shows the listener’s gender.

you.m: Asked of you: kiedy byłeś młody?
you.f: Asked of you: kiedy byłaś młoda?

mloda.why: An adjective after być stays in the nominative (byłaś młoda), whereas a noun would be instrumental (byłaś studentką).

you.m: Asked of you: kiedy byłeś młody?
you.f: Asked of you: kiedy byłaś młoda?

mieszkalismy.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 1st person plural · virile
mieszkalismy.why: Imperfective: a long-term situation. Virile, because the family included men.

you.f: With a mixed group: mieszkaliśmy. Only women: mieszkałyśmy.

parts: irregular: wieś loses its e in all other forms
wsi.why: Wieś drops its vowel in every form but the nominative and accusative: wsi, wsią. “In the countryside” is na wsi, with na.

przy.why: Przy + locative: przy stole, “at the table.” Na stole would mean on top of it.

siadalo.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 3rd person singular · neuter
siadalo.why: With a collective numeral, or any numeral from five up, as its subject, a past verb is neuter singular: siadało nas czternaścioro. Imperfective, because it happened every Sunday.

czternascioro.why: A collective numeral, used for a mixed group of men, women and children. Nas, “of us”, is genitive.

jedlismy.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 1st person plural · virile
parts: past stem of jeść (jed- before l)
jedlismy.why: Jeść has two past stems: jad- before ł (jadł, jadłam) and jed- before l (jedli, jedliśmy). Imperfective: a habit.

niedziele.why: Days of the week take w + accusative: w niedzielę.

wstawala.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 3rd person singular · feminine
wstawala.why: Imperfective for something that happened regularly. The perfective wstała would describe a single morning.

piatej.why: Clock times are feminine ordinals agreeing with an understood godzina. “At” a time is o + locative: o piątej, “at five.”

zeby.why: Żeby + infinitive expresses purpose when the subject stays the same: wstawała, żeby upiec chleb, “got up to bake bread.”

upiec.why: Piec belongs to a small group of verbs whose infinitive ends in -c instead of -ć: piec, móc, biec. The perfective u- means baking it all the way through.

opowiadal.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 3rd person singular · masculine

te.why: The feminine accusative of ten is tę: tę samą historię. In everyday speech you’ll often hear tą, but tę is the standard form.

historie.why: Direct object of opowiadał. Historia means both “story” and “history.”

wojsku.why: O + locative, “about.” Stems ending in k take -u: o wojsku.

razem.why: Za każdym razem, “every time”, is a fixed phrase with za + instrumental. On its own, razem means “together.”

zeby2.why: When the subject changes, żeby takes a bare past form instead of an infinitive: lubił, żeby wszyscy słuchali, “he liked everyone to listen.”

wszyscy.why: Wszyscy is used for “everyone” when the group includes men. For a group of women, or of things, it’s wszystkie.

sluchali.tags: verb · imperfective · past form · 3rd person plural · virile
sluchali.why: After żeby, a bare past form agreeing with wszyscy. Słuchać takes the genitive: słuchać kogoś, hence go.

wezmie.why: Wziąć is irregular: future wezmę, weźmiesz, weźmie; past wziął, wzięła. Wziąć do ręki, “to pick up.”

reki.why: Do + genitive. Ręka is irregular in the plural (ręce) and has an old locative, w ręku, alongside w ręce.

parts: verb stem; 3rd sg. has no ending
zmywa.why: Kto…, ten… means “whoever…, (they)…”. The present tense states a general rule. Zmywać naczynia is “to do the washing-up.”

przegrala.tags: verb · perfective · past · 3rd person singular · feminine
przegrala.why: Grać is “to play”; przegrać is “to lose” and wygrać “to win.” Feminine, for Kasia.

sprawdzalam.tags: verb · imperfective · past · 1st person singular · feminine
sprawdzalam.why: Imperfective: Kasia presents what she was doing as an activity in progress, which sounds more innocent than the perfective sprawdziłam.

przepis.tags: noun · masculine inanimate · accusative singular (same as nominative)
przepis.why: Przepis means both “recipe” and “regulation”, something written down. A recipe for something is przepis na + accusative.

exercises.prompt: “The cakes looked delicious” (ciasta, wyglądać): Ciasta ___ pysznie.
exercises.explain: Ciasta aren’t people, so non-virile: wygląda + ł + y.
Before l the stem is jed-: jed + l + i.
exercises.hint: Jadł but jedliśmy: which stem goes before l?

exercises.explain: O + the locative of the feminine ordinal: o siódmej.

exercises.prompt: “I want you (a man) to stay” (zostać): Chcę, żebyś ___.
exercises.explain: The person marker is already on żebyś, so the verb is a bare past form: zosta + ł.

exercises.prompt: Say about yourself: “I was only reading” (czytać): Ja tylko ___.

explain.m: Imperfective, with the masculine inserted e: czyta + ł + e + m.

exercises.hint: Compare sprawdzałam, and check the learner setting at the top.
